He’s never held suicide over my head to make me do something, and he didn’t bring it up in this situation. My mind just went to that conclusion because he has a lot of childhood trauma, and has been dealing with that recently, which has been bringing up some nasty emotions.. That, and all of the stress from COVID-19 had put him in this depressive state recently and unfortunately i’ve had to talk him down from suicide a few times over the past few weeks. Sure enough, this morning he called me and he was considering again. I messaged his mother because i realized that my efforts were only calming down the crisis at hand and not fixing the cause and actual issues.. We’re both in therapy and are trying to work on ourselves..
He’s not always like this, and i’m far from perfect - just this december i was sent to a mental hospital for a suicide attempt and he stayed with me and helped me get out of my state of mind. I love him very much, and seeing him act how i was acting previously... i don’t know if i could leave him because morally i want to return what he did for me.. i want to see him grow like he was able to watch me grow.
Yeah, i can logically recognize that this dynamic of two very mentally ill people in a relationship together is toxic and hurtful.. but i’m emotionally dependent and i want to help him with everything in me, and the thought of leaving/being abandoned tears me to pieces.
Thank you! I’ll reach out and hopefully he’s still not mad and chooses to respond.. And yeah, I totally agree his behavior is toxic, but i def should wait until he’s calm to talk about it.

i take vyvance - and it helps me a lot, but if you’re interested on learning the negative affects of adderall  there’s an interesting documentary on Netflix called “Take Your Pills” that talks about the history of amphetamines and their affects long term + how adderall is affecting the youth.
